data.name: AlFatah
data.gender_notes: AlFatah is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: AlFatah is a name derived from the Arabic word 'fatha', meaning 'opener' or 'conqueror'. In Islamic history, Al-Fath bin Al-Abbas was an influential companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and was known for his bravery and wisdom. The name AlFatah carries the meaning “Opener, Conqueror” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose AlFatah usually hope their child will grow to embody opener, conqueror and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of AlFatah total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name AlFatah holds deep significance in Islamic history, as it was given to the first major military victory of Islam. The conquest of the city of Khaybar in 628 AD, led by the Prophet Muhammad himself, is known as the Battle of AlFath. This victory provided sustenance and financial resources for the Muslim community, and is celebrated as a symbol of Islamic power and resilience.
